subtitle: Vaan takes command in the sky

body: Final Fantasy XII: Revenant Wings is Think & Feel and Square Enix's Nintendo DS strategy adventure following Vaan and Penelo after their earlier journey. Their life as sky pirates leads them into a conflict around the floating continent of Lemurés. The player commands groups of summoned creatures in real time, giving the familiar characters a different role on the battlefield. An airship connects destinations and missions. The world of Ivalice returns through a smaller machine, but the central task is now directing a force rather than controlling one fighter's immediate actions.

Commanders lead squads across mission maps, and the touchscreen makes selecting a group and directing its movement a physical gesture. Different objectives give the force something more specific to do than simply clear every opponent. The summoned creatures provide the units through which those orders take effect. A useful plan depends on bringing the appropriate group to the right place while the battle continues. The handheld format makes this a compact interpretation of real-time strategy, with the player watching several small actions develop from a sequence of direct orders.

The airship gradually becomes more than a way to choose the next destination. Shops provide equipment and materials, while an artificer can turn resources collected during missions into useful items. Preparation therefore returns to a shared place between encounters. Much of the music arranges Hitoshi Sakimoto's Final Fantasy XII score, with new pieces by Kenichiro Fukui linking the change of genre to the earlier adventure. Revenant Wings gives its continuation a distinct purpose: familiar people and sounds support a new way of organising action in Ivalice.
